ruleset.name: jpinpoint-nextgen-rules
ruleset.description: jPinpoint "nextgen" rule set: new Kotlin concurrent rules using PMD 7.28.0 type-resolution XPath functions (pmd-kotlin:typeIs, pmd-kotlin:hasAnnotation, pmd-kotlin:matchesSig). These rules REQUIRE a PMD version that supports those features and therefore are NOT included in the standard jpinpoint-kotlin-rules.xml, to keep that file working on older PMD versions. See the "Nextgen rules" section in the README for details. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: SynchronizingForLocalVars
rule.description: Problem: Synchronizing a block that only accesses local variables adds locking overhead without protecting shared state. Solution: Only synchronize when the block accesses shared mutable state. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidCompletionServiceTake
rule.description: Problem: take() stalls indefinitely in case of hanging threads and consumes a thread. Solution: use poll() with a timeout value and handle the timeout. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidFutureGetWithoutTimeout
rule.description: Problem: Stalls indefinitely in case of hanging threads and consumes a thread. Solution: Provide a timeout value and handle the timeout. (jpinpoint-rules)

property.name: xpath

rule.name: AvoidCommonPoolForBlockingCalls
rule.message: Avoid parallelStream() for blocking (remote) calls; it uses the ForkJoinPool common pool which can starve other tasks.
rule.description: Problem: parallelStream() uses the ForkJoinPool common pool (shared JVM-wide). Blocking calls (HTTP, DB) starve it. Solution: Use a dedicated ForkJoinPool (submit your parallel work to it), or use Kotlin coroutines with IO dispatcher. (jpinpoint-rules)

property.name: xpath

rule.name: AvoidExecutorInvokeWithoutTimeout
rule.message: Avoid using ExecutorService::invokeAll or invokeAny without a timeout.
rule.description: Problem: Stalls indefinitely in case of stalled Callable(s) and consumes threads. Solution: Provide a timeout to the invokeAll/invokeAny method and handle the timeout. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidParallelStreamWithCommonPool
rule.message: Beware: parallelStream with the common pool is rarely a good choice.
rule.description: Problem: Collection.parallelStream uses the common pool, with #threads = #CPUs. It is designed to distribute much CPU work over the cores. It is not designed for remote calls or other blocking calls. In addition, parallelizing has CPU overhead and concurrency risks. Solution: Prefer sequential streams or Kotlin sequences, or use a dedicated pool when parallelism is justified. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidFutureJoinWithoutTimeout
rule.description: Problem: Stalls indefinitely in case of hanging thread(s) and consumes a thread. Solution: Provide a timeout before the join and handle the timeout. For example a future.get(timeout, unit), an orTimeout() or a completeOnTimeout(). You may want to use CompletableFuture.allOf() too. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidUnguardedAssignmentToNonFinalFieldsInSharedObjects
rule.message: Avoid unguarded assignments to non-final fields in objects shared among threads. Access thread-safely AND use @GuardedBy.
rule.description: Problem: Multiple threads typically access fields of a singleton or may access fields in session scoped objects. Unguarded assignment to a non-final (var) field is thread-unsafe and may cause corruption or visibility problems. It may also unintentionally mix-up session data. Solution: Make the properties val and unmodifiable. If they really need to be mutable, make access thread-safe: use @Synchronized and @GuardedBy or @Volatile. Notes 1. For autowiring/injection, the assignment of the reference is thread safe, so var is acceptable. The unmodifiable/thread-safe requirement for that field still holds. Also make sure no other thread-unsafe assignment is made to that field. 2. In case you are sure the Component is used in single threaded context only (e.g. a Tasklet), annotate the class with @NotThreadSafe to make this explicit. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidCommonPoolForFutureAsync
rule.message: Avoid using the common thread pool for future.supplyAsync, use a separate pool.
rule.description: Problem: CompletableFuture.supplyAsync is typically used for remote calls. By default, it uses the common pool. The number of threads in the common pool is equal to the number of CPUs, which is suitable for in-memory processing. For I/O, however, this number is typically not suitable because most time is spent waiting for the response and not in CPU. The common pool must not be used for blocking calls. Solution: A separate, properly sized, pool of threads (an Executor) should be used for the async calls. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidUnguardedAssignmentToNonFinalFieldsInObjectsUsingSynchronized
rule.message: Avoid unguarded assignments to non-final fields in objects using synchronized. Access thread-safely AND use @GuardedBy.
rule.description: Problem: Multiple threads typically access fields of an object using synchronized. Unguarded assignment to a non-final (var) field is thread-unsafe and may cause corruption or visibility problems. To make this thread-safe, that is, guard the field e.g. with @Synchronized methods, may cause contention. Solution: Make the properties val and unmodifiable. If they really need to be mutable, make access thread-safe: use @Synchronized and @GuardedBy or @Volatile. Notes: 1. In case you are sure the class is used in a single threaded context only, remove the current use of synchronized and annotate the class with @NotThreadSafe to make this explicit. 2. Use @VisibleForTesting for methods (e.g. setters) used for JUnit only. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidNonPrivateFieldsInSharedObjects
rule.message: Avoid non-private properties in shared objects. Make properties private to ensure thread-safety.
rule.description: Problem: A singleton, or more general: an object shared among threads, has a property that is not private. These properties can possibly be modified from other classes. Solution: Make the properties private. Note: properties are excluded when annotated with: @Autowired/@Value/@Inject. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidUnguardedMutableFieldsInSharedObjects
rule.message: Avoid unguarded non-final or mutable fields in objects shared among threads. Make final immutable or access thread-safely AND use @GuardedBy.
rule.description: Problem: Multiple threads typically access fields of a singleton or may access fields in session scoped objects. If a field or its reference is mutable, access is thread-unsafe and may cause corruption or visibility problems. It may also unintentionally mix-up session data. Solution: Make the properties val and unmodifiable. If they really need to be mutable, make access thread-safe: use @Synchronized and @GuardedBy or @Volatile. Notes: 1. Instances of Date, StringBuilder, URL and File are examples of mutable objects and should be avoided (or else guarded) as fields of shared objects. 2. Instances of classes like ArrayList, HashMap and HashSet are also mutable and should be properly wrapped with e.g. Collections.unmodifiableList after initialization, or use thread-safe implementations like ConcurrentHashMap. 3. For autowiring/injection, the assignment of the reference is thread safe, so var is acceptable. The unmodifiable/thread-safe requirement for that field still holds. 4. In case you are sure the Component is used in single threaded context only, annotate the class with @NotThreadSafe to make this explicit. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidMutableStaticFields
rule.message: Avoid mutable static fields. Make val (immutable) or use thread-safe access with @Volatile or @GuardedBy.
rule.description: Problem: Multiple threads typically access static fields. Unguarded assignment to a mutable or non-final static field is thread-unsafe and may cause corruption or visibility problems. To make this thread-safe, that is, guard the field e.g. with synchronized methods, may cause contention. Solution: Make the fields final and unmodifiable. If they really need to be mutable, make access thread-safe: use synchronized and @GuardedBy, use volatile or a suitable concurrent collection type. Consider lock contention. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidStaticXmlFactories
rule.message: XML Factory is used as static/object/companion field. XML factories are not thread-safe. Use local variables instead.
rule.description: An XML Factory like DocumentBuilderFactory, TransformerFactory, MessageFactory is used as static field. Problem: These factory objects are typically not thread-safe and rather expensive to create because of class loading.
